body: The US Air Force is looking at enclosing six F-35A parking shelters at Tyndall Air Force Base, Florida, with protective netting designed to keep small drones away from parked fighters and the personnel working on them. A sources sought notice published on SAM.gov on November 6, 2026, asks contractors to design, supply and install counter-unmanned aircraft system (C-UAS) netting on all four sides of the existing sunshade structures. The notice is part of a market research effort and does not commit the service to a purchase.

Each sunshade measures approximately 192 meters (630 feet) long, 20 meters (65 feet) wide and nine meters (30 feet) high, with six bays per structure, according to the notice. Design drawings prepared for the US Army Corps of Engineers' Mobile District in 2023 show two F-35As parked side by side in a typical bay, giving the six structures room for up to 72 fighters, matching the number the Air Force planned to assign to Tyndall's 325th Fighter Wing when it selected the base to host three F-35A squadrons in March 2021.

The netting must be capable of stopping Group 1 drones, the smallest category in the US military's classification, covering aircraft weighing up to approximately nine kilograms (20 pounds). The Air Force specifies UV- and moisture-resistant material capable of withstanding temperatures of up to 204 degrees Celsius (400 degrees Fahrenheit), mesh openings no larger than 7.6 centimeters (three inches), and a minimum tensile strength of 91 kilograms (200 pounds). The system must also meet Miami-Dade County wind-load requirements. The north and south faces, where aircraft enter and exit the shelters, must be fitted with netting that can be quickly retracted without disrupting normal flight-line operations. Contractors are also asked to assess whether the existing metal structures can support the additional loads, and the notice encourages small businesses to respond.

Tyndall is not the first US fighter base to consider protective netting. In October 2024, Langley Air Force Base, Virginia, sought a prototype installation for one of 42 F-22 Raptor sunshades, following a series of unexplained drone incursions in December 2023. The vulnerability of parked aircraft was demonstrated on June 1, 2025, when Ukraine launched Operation Spiderweb, using small first-person-view (FPV) drones concealed in trucks to strike Russian military air bases; a subsequent US Department of Defense report, citing the Defense Intelligence Agency, assessed that at least 10 Russian strategic bombers were destroyed. In January 2026, Joint Interagency Task Force 401 published recommendations that include netting and tensioned cables to prevent small drones from reaching critical infrastructure.
en.summary: The US Air Force is seeking counter-drone netting for six F-35A parking shelters at Tyndall Air Force Base, Florida, under a November 6 sources sought notice that asks contractors to enclose the sunshades on all four sides. The netting must stop Group 1 drones of up to about nine kilograms.
en.title: US Air Force seeks anti-drone nets for F-35A shelters at Tyndall

body: 美國空軍正考慮為佛羅里達州廷德爾空軍基地的6座F-35A停機棚加裝防護網，以防小型無人機接近停放的戰機與在旁作業的人員。美國空軍於2026年11月6日在SAM.gov發布徵求來源公告，請廠商為現有遮陽棚結構四面設計、供應並安裝反無人機系統（C-UAS）防護網；該公告屬於市場調查，不代表軍方承諾採購。
根據公告，每座遮陽棚長約192公尺、寬約20公尺、高約9公尺，各有6個停機位。美國陸軍工兵部隊莫比爾分區2023年準備的設計圖顯示，一個典型停機位可並排停放2架F-35A；6座結構合計可容納最多72架戰機，與美國空軍2021年3月選定廷德爾基地進駐3個F-35A中隊時，規劃配屬第325戰鬥機聯隊的數量相符。
防護網必須能攔截第1類無人機，也就是美軍分類中最小的類別，涵蓋重量約9公斤以下的航空器。美國空軍要求材質抗紫外線、防潮，可耐攝氏204度高溫，網孔不得大於7.6公分，最低抗拉強度91公斤，並須符合邁阿密-戴德縣的風載要求。戰機進出的南北兩面須裝設可快速收起的防護網，以免干擾正常的飛行線作業。公告也請廠商評估現有金屬結構能否承受新增負載、是否需要改裝，並鼓勵小型企業投標。

廷德爾並非首座考慮防護網的美國戰機基地。2024年10月，維吉尼亞州蘭利空軍基地曾為42座F-22遮陽棚中的一座徵求原型安裝案，起因是2023年12月發生一連串不明無人機入侵事件。停放航空器的脆弱性在2025年6月1日烏克蘭發動「蛛網行動」時得到印證：烏方以藏於卡車內的小型第一人稱視角（FPV）無人機攻擊俄羅斯軍用機場；美國國防部其後援引國防情報局的報告評估，至少10架俄羅斯戰略轟炸機被摧毀。2026年1月，第401聯合跨部會特遣隊發布的建議亦包括以防護網與張力纜線防止小型無人機接近關鍵基礎設施。
zh.summary: 美國空軍11月6日發布徵求來源公告，擬為佛羅里達州廷德爾空軍基地6座F-35A停機棚四面加裝反無人機防護網，須能攔截約9公斤以下的第1類無人機；該公告屬於市場調查，尚未承諾採購。
zh.title: 美軍擬為廷德爾基地F-35A機棚加裝反無人機防護網
